name: Deep Lake
tagline: Activeloop's tensor-native data engine for AI: vectors, multimodal data and versioning on object storage.
description: Deep Lake started as Activeloop's 'Hub' format for streaming ML datasets to PyTorch and grew into a database for AI that stores tensors, embeddings, images, video and text on object storage with git-like version control. Version 4 rewrote the core in C++ with vector and BM25 indexes and a Tensor Query Language, and Activeloop now positions it as a data runtime for agents with a serverless Postgres interface. It is most compelling when the same multimodal data is used for both model training and retrieval; as a pure vector store it is less common than Qdrant or Chroma.

pricing.notes: Library is free with your own storage; Activeloop's managed Deeplake service and enterprise plans are priced via the Activeloop app/sales.

scale.notes: Data lives in S3/GCS/Azure Blob; compute streams chunks on demand, so dataset size is bounded by object storage.

strengths: Stores raw multimodal data and embeddings together on object storage
Git-like branching and version history for datasets
Streams data directly into PyTorch/TensorFlow training loops
Vector and BM25 indexes in the same tables
weaknesses: Shifting product positioning makes long-term roadmap harder to judge
Smaller vector-DB community and fewer framework integrations than rivals
Major-version format changes (v3 to v4) required migrations
useCases: Multimodal datasets shared by training and RAG
Agent memory over documents and images
notIdealFor: Simple text-only vector search where Chroma or pgvector suffice
